_doc: Per-runtime facts used by plan.py. Versions were READ in the official runtime pages on 2026-10-24 (https://www.clever.cloud/developers/doc/deploy/applications/<runtime>/index.html.md) — re-read the page before relying on them; plan.py labels them [read doc 2026-10-24].

node.start: package.json scripts.start or main; CC_RUN_COMMAND overrides
node.build_hook: CC_POST_BUILD_HOOK="<pm> run build" — the runtime runs install, NOT build
node.dev_deps: CC_NODE_DEV_DEPENDENCIES=install when build tools sit in devDependencies

python.uv: native uv mode only when uv.lock is at the root AND CC_PYTHON_UV_RUN_COMMAND is set: uv.lock alone falls back to the legacy mode, which fails without requirements.txt and CC_PYTHON_MODULE (test T4, 2026-10-26). CC_PYTHON_MODULE and CC_PYTHON_BACKEND are then ignored and the command is not run by a shell (no $VAR, no expansion: documentation read 2026-10-25, consistent with test T5 where the port had to be written): none of the two is set; gunicorn reads PORT itself (`uv run --no-sync gunicorn <module>`, no --bind), uvicorn is given the port (`uv run --no-sync uvicorn --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 <module>`). `uv run --no-sync`: without --no-sync every start re-syncs the environment, dev group included (about 50 MB downloaded per instance start, test T5). The interpreter follows requires-python (>=3.14 gave CPython 3.14.8 although the build log says 'Using Python version 3.13'), so CC_PYTHON_VERSION is not set. A uv workspace with a virtual root deploys the same way (the member is installed by uv sync, test T5)
python.start: CC_PYTHON_MODULE="module:app" behind CC_PYTHON_BACKEND (daphne, gunicorn, uvicorn, uwsgi; default uwsgi). With CC_RUN_COMMAND the app must listen on 9000.
python.django: legacy mode: CC_PYTHON_MANAGE_TASKS="migrate --no-input, collectstatic --noinput" runs during the BUILD, once per build even with 2 instances, and reaches the linked add-on (test T2, 2026-10-26). uv mode: CC_PYTHON_MANAGE_TASKS is NOT run — `CC_POST_BUILD_HOOK="uv run --no-sync python manage.py migrate --noinput"` runs once per deploy, whatever the number of instances, and joins the linked add-on (tests T4, T5)
python.forwarded: FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS=* with gunicorn or uvicorn: behind Clever's proxy, without it a redirect leaves as http:// instead of https:// (test T5, 2026-10-26: 307 with location http://… until the variable was set)
observed: 2026-10-25 (validation round 1): with CC_PYTHON_MODULE + CC_PYTHON_BACKEND=gunicorn, Clever binds gunicorn to 127.0.0.1:9000 behind nginx (public 8080), ignores `bind` from gunicorn.conf.py and starts 2 workers; worker_class from gunicorn.conf.py is applied
2026-10-25 (validation round 1): migrate in CC_PYTHON_MANAGE_TASKS reached the linked PostgreSQL add-on at build time ('Applying …' lines in the build log)

2026-10-26 (test T4): uv.lock alone = legacy mode and a failed build; with CC_PYTHON_UV_RUN_COMMAND the build ran `uv sync --locked --no-progress --no-dev`; CC_POST_BUILD_HOOK ran migrate on the linked add-on; psycopg 3 (pure) found the system libpq; --addon-version 16 gave PostgreSQL 16.15

2026-10-26 (test T5): `uv run` without --no-sync re-downloaded the dev group at every start; FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS=* turned http:// redirects into https://; CC_POST_BUILD_HOOK ran once per deploy, CC_PRE_RUN_HOOK once per instance
2026-10-26 (test T2): Celery's native variables keep HTTP on 8080 (nginx to gunicorn on 9000); CC_PYTHON_CELERY_USE_BEAT starts one beat per instance, with no lock, whatever the scheduler

dotnet.note: non-LTS and older versions are not supported; ASPNETCORE_URLS=http://0.0.0.0:8080 is preset; CC_DOTNET_PROJ when several project files
observed: 2026-10-25: NuGet restore on Clever's .NET build VM fails with NU3018 'signing certificate is not trusted by the trust provider', reproduced 4/4 (SDK 8.0.132, the VM's code-signing trust chain; a local SDK 8.0.131 restores the same project fine) → DOTNET_NUGET_SIGNATURE_VERIFICATION=false set before the first build, kept until the platform is fixed (it disables NuGet signature verification on the build VM); NU3042 warnings are noise

go.build: CC_GO_BUILD_TOOL gomod (go.mod at the root: the module read from go.mod is passed to go install) | gobuild | makefile (CC_GO_BINARY); CC_GO_PKG = package path passed to go install, overrides the module — needed when main is not at the module root; listen on 0.0.0.0:8080 [read doc 2026-10-25]

php.note: CC_WEBROOT=/public for Laravel/Symfony (absolute from the project root; relative or '..' fails the deploy) [read doc 2026-10-25]
php.composer: composer install at build when composer.json is at the root [read doc 2026-10-25]

static.note: Node 24, npm 11 and Bun 1.4.3 are available at build (test T5, 2026-10-26): CC_BUILD_COMMAND can call npm, node or bun without a mise.toml. SPA fallback needs a Caddyfile at the root (taken into account automatically, no CC_STATIC_SERVER needed: `:8080 { root * <webroot> ; encode gzip ; try_files {path} /index.html ; file_server }`); without it, or SERVER_FALLBACK_PAGE, a deep link answers 404 on the default server (SWS), which also caches js/css for a year. The Caddyfile fallback answers 200 with index.html for any missing file; the SWS fallback does not answer HEAD requests. CC_WEBROOT shrinks the build cache (473 MB without, 920 KB with, test T5)
static.build: CC_BUILD_COMMAND runs during the build if set; else auto-build of supported generators (Astro, Docusaurus, Nuxt, VitePress) into cc_static_autobuilt; CC_WEBROOT (default /); a root Caddyfile is used with Caddy [read doc 2026-10-25]. A Vite front built with Bun on pico: 17 s, no instance of its own for the build (test T5)

docker.note: one container per app; CMD/ENTRYPOINT required; CC_RUN_COMMAND ignored; PORT=8080 imposed; no workers, cron or FS Bucket

platform.hooks: CC_PRE_BUILD_HOOK (before dependencies), CC_POST_BUILD_HOOK (after the build, before the cache), CC_PRE_RUN_HOOK (before the start, on EVERY deploy) — a failing one fails the deploy; CC_RUN_SUCCEEDED_HOOK / CC_RUN_FAILED_HOOK do not [read doc 2026-10-25]
platform.workers_doc: CC_WORKER_COMMAND, or CC_WORKER_COMMAND_0, _1…; CC_WORKER_RESTART always|on-failure (default)|no; not available for Docker apps [read doc 2026-10-25]
platform.listen: 0.0.0.0:$PORT (8080); a service must listen on 8080 before any HTTP check, so a process with no HTTP server cannot be an app on its own as is
platform.health_check: default GET / and any 200-499 passes (a 400 page passes the deploy!); CC_HEALTH_CHECK_PATH makes it strict 2xx
platform.workers: CC_WORKER_COMMAND[_n] next to the web process on the same app (not with Docker)
platform.cron: clevercloud/cron.json: a JSON array of "<cron expr> $ROOT/clevercloud/cron-job.sh METHOD /path" ($ROOT is substituted); jobs run on EVERY instance with an EMPTY environment (no app variables, no INSTANCE_NUMBER, no PORT): templates/cron/cron-env.sh (CC_PRE_RUN_HOOK) writes them to a 600 git-ignored file, templates/cron/cron-job.sh sources it, runs only on the app that carries CRON_RUNS_HERE=1 (cron.json is deployed to every app built from the repository; elsewhere the job exits 0 with one line), on instance 0 only, and sends the secret from a 600 header file; output in clever logs (CMD/CMDOUT/CMDEND); not with Docker
platform.zero_downtime: ON by default on an app created with clever-tools 5.2.0: check it with `clever config get zero-downtime` before promising anything and do not present it as an action; change it with `clever config set zero-downtime true|false`; the enable and disable options of `clever config update` answer 'No configuration to update' and change nothing (test T6, 2026-10-26). Off: a redeploy answers 503 for the whole build and start (1 min 46 measured, with 2 instances too); on: 0 error in 3 runs at 1 request per second, with 1 instance as with 2
platform.env_values: Clever does not expand $VAR in the value of an environment variable: the app receives the literal text (test T1, 2026-10-25). CC_RUN_COMMAND is run by a shell, which expands $PORT and $REDIS_URL: a command that needs another variable goes there (CC_RUN_COMMAND='<start> --flag="$REDIS_URL"'); the hooks are run by a shell too (test T5); CC_PYTHON_UV_RUN_COMMAND is not (test T5): no $VAR in it. Or read the variable in the code
platform.hooks_once: CC_POST_BUILD_HOOK runs once per deploy, whatever the number of instances, and sees the linked add-on; CC_PRE_RUN_HOOK runs once per instance (tests T2, T5, 2026-10-26): migrations go in CC_POST_BUILD_HOOK
platform.singletons: Celery beat starts on every instance, with no lock, whatever the scheduler: N instances run each periodic task N times, and the old instances stay about 2 min after a deploy (test T2, 2026-10-26). A beat, cron or scheduler process runs in an app of its own, with one instance (min == max == 1); the tasks stay idempotent; the main worker stays on the web app (the native Celery variables also start a small one next to the beat, test T2). The web app keeps its migrations; the new app gets the web app's secrets COPIED (never generated twice), is deployed last, has its default domain removed after its first deploy, and runs the repository's cron jobs nowhere (CRON_RUNS_HERE=1 is on the designated app only). Not measured on such an app: the split itself
platform.autoscaling: scale-up about 53 s after a sustained CPU load starts (the new instance is up about 80 s after), scale-down about 11 min 30 after it ends; one measurement (test T1, 2026-10-25): a known event is pre-scaled at H-1 (clever scale --min-instances <n> before it, back after), never left to the autoscaler alone
platform.redis_eviction: [read doc 2026-10-25] Redis eviction policy: noeviction by default; LRU needs a ticket to Clever support. A full cache refuses writes: right for a queue, not for a cache
platform.path_routing: clever domain add <fqdn>/<path> routes to the app only the requests whose path starts with the prefix, read as a plain string, the safe side (T1 did not test whether a segment boundary is required, so /en is taken to route /env and /print to route /printenv); every other path gets the router's own 404. Add the prefixes the app serves, THEN remove the default domain with clever domain rm: never the other way round. No prefix may cover a closed path, and the prefix / covers everything. /env, / and the ..-variants ended in 404 (test T1, 2026-10-25); the Request Flow was not tested
